That helper always applies shared gravity using pokemon_spawn.x1C/x20; when its existing x24 countdown is positive it decrements the countdown and returns false, while a non-positive countdown causes model-scale restoration and a true result. False skips only this wrapper's transition block, not all object mutation. facts.value: Initializes a swarm member and enters its local active state 0. If abs(vel.x) is strictly greater than abs(vel.y), it multiplies vel.y by attr->x1C.f and stores selector 0; otherwise, including ties, it multiplies vel.x and stores selector 1. It clears the three angle accumulators and initializes independent angular increments from attribute-derived random ranges. Active physics advances those angles and multiplies the stored-selector component by attr->x20.f without recomputing the dominant axis. These operations attenuate or align motion only for suitable attribute values. The separate animation callback decrements lifetime and returns true at zero or below; collision always returns false.

evidence.why: Lead initialization, random sign selection, route and counter uses.
Descriptor inheritance and independent child state.

facts.rationale: Separates inherited descriptor data from child-local attribute initialization and preserves distinct meanings of shared union storage across the two item lifetimes. Also distinguishes random acceleration-sign selection from attribute-derived values.
facts.value: Lead initialization randomly selects one of 26 attribute-provided forms and a separate ±1 acceleration sign, sets the emission interval to zero and loads the remaining-emission count from attributes; blast-zone coordinates, camera interest and lead speed attributes determine a stored route. Each emission descriptor carries randomized route-anchor coordinates, the stored velocity, facing, owner and lead-object parent reference. The child's own special attributes and fresh random draws independently initialize its form, lifetime and angular increments. Lead fields x64/x68 serve as integer emission counters, whereas child fields at those positions are floating-point angle accumulators; x78 similarly holds a lead route vector versus a child axis selector. Both item kinds delegate matching interaction-reference removal to the common cleanup helper.
